recommendation: Reserve rather than immediately benchmark: prioritize belief-directed native goals. Eight weighted worlds offer only one or two lower-quarter tail observations.
hypothesis: Use lower-tail continuation value to avoid actions whose average depends on favorable hidden armies. This changes the objective, rather than estimating standard errors or randomizing moves.

fixed_candidate_if_later_tested.reason: A predeclared lower quartile is a transparent moderately adverse tail, equivalent to at-most fourfold probability reweighting. Literature supports the family, not this game-specific optimum. Alpha is fixed before outcome evidence.
fixed_candidate_if_later_tested.weighted_atoms: Sort X ascending; take exactly alpha of normalized probability mass, splitting the boundary atom fractionally; divide its weighted sum by alpha.
preserve: same eight weighted worlds and masked continuations
same immediate known wins and parent tie rule
same correction clip, coefficients and mean reference
fixed_candidate_if_later_tested.cost: O(actions*samples*log(samples)), zero extra rollouts; raw per-world values must be retained.

algebra_caveat: A per-world reference is random, even though it is action-independent. CVaR(X-reference) is not CVaR(X)-mean(reference); including it in the tail changes which worlds are adverse and introduces risk relative to an imaginary pass. Keeping mean(reference) isolates risk of the action continuation.
limits: future-immediate is a heuristic continuation correction, not actual game return. Immediate uncertain Flag wins cancel in the existing architecture; CVaR does not repair that omission.
Repeated fixed-alpha root replanning is not an implementation of time-consistent dynamic CVaR. Risk budget/state augmentation and belief updates would be needed for stronger claims.
Importance-weighted finite empirical tails do not inherit independent-sample concentration guarantees directly. Model misspecification, sparse hidden Flag events and eight worlds remain material.
A lower tail can reject useful sacrifices and draws in lost positions; literature does not guarantee more wins.

historical_resolution.matching: Original public prefixes, sampler RNG streams and all saved effective sample sizes reproduced without continuations or outcome tuning.

sources.supports: Section2 CVaR and bounded probability reweighting; Section3 augmented risk state for dynamic programming. Root empirical adaptation here is an inference, not their algorithm.
